blacklistabilityReview.evidence: EURSPKCC is issued through permissioned fund or issuer rails with KYC-gated primary-market access and issuer/admin controls over transfer, mint, redemption, or token administration.

oracleRisk.summary: EURSPKCC publishes its euro-denominated fund NAV through a permissioned Spiko AggregatorV3-compatible oracle; the fund reports profit and loss daily, so this is a single administrative valuation path rather than a live liquidation feed.

branchApplicability.rationale: EURSPKCC represents shares in one professionally managed cash-and-carry fund. Investors submit fund-share redemption requests that an authorized operator executes by burning the shares; they do not open borrower-specific collateral positions, and the reviewed contracts expose no permissionless liquidation markets to split into branches.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: EURSPKCC has six issuer-native deployments. Chainlink CCIP spans the four EVM native deployments with twelve current directed lanes, using BurnWithFromMintTokenPool 1.6.1 burn-and-mint: source pool-held EURSPKCC is burned and destination mint is admitted only after CCIP RMN, authorized OffRamp, configured source-pool, and inbound-rate-limiter validation, with per-lane rate limits and remote pool/token mappings. The pools are administered by the shared EOA 0xEd608cf38968C0ba09676843D90B33Dd59dd7375, which can update peers and rate-limit configuration; those controls are bridge-route risk, not canonical native Mint Authority. Starknet and Stellar are not CCIP routes.

controls.label: EURSPKCC shared CCIP pool owner EOA

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: At the four current pool-read heads, the same owner controls each pool's configured remote pool/token mappings across all twelve directed EVM lanes.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The owner can call setChainRateLimiterConfig on each pool and can widen or remove the per-lane bridge-mint bounds.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The owner can call applyChainUpdates on each pool for remote lane administration; eth_getCode(owner) = 0x on the Ethereum observation and the same EOA address is returned by all four current pool reads.

controls.capDescription: A single EOA owns the four CCIP pools and can administer peer mappings and per-lane rate-limit configuration, but it is not a direct caller of the native token mint function.
bypassSurfaces: The shared EOA is a common-mode bridge failure domain across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Base; CCIP RMN, OffRamp, source-pool, and burn accounting checks remain route invariants.
controls.evidence: Current pool reads on 2026-08-16 identify owner 0xEd608cf38968C0ba09676843D90B33Dd59dd7375 for Ethereum block 25770462, Polygon block 92141614, Arbitrum block 495274659, and Base block 50064051. The owner is an EOA (Ethereum eth_getCode = 0x) and its reviewed powers are applyChainUpdates and setChainRateLimiterConfig across the four pools.
